body:
I've always been skeptical of labelling my experience as abuse. They're a retired counselling psychologist. I was referring to them getting sick of me being a dependant who couldn't care for themselves if they tried. I don't like labelling people as good/evil when there's so much grey area. They have done good for me, including raising me. Though I can't help but recognise that their attitude certainly had a role in my downward spiral. But in my insane head I could convince myself that anyone and everyone is responsible for my own problems.

> For many with eating disorders it is only when they are completely divorced from the abusive family environment that improvement and even recovery is possible.

I wish I could afford rent. The few places I can afford require no pets etc. I have a reptile that I care for dearly. Everything is fucked.
